sys-apps/upstart: clean up created domain sockets on exit We don't want to leave leftover sockets we created, since will causes us problems if we ever have to respawn this daemon (we'll see "address in use"). BUG=chromium:616778 TEST=`start upstart-socket-bridge; stop upstart-socket-bridge`; check that domain sockets (e.g., /run/cups/cups.sock, once CUPS gets support for this) get removed. Also, try `restart upstart-socket-bridge` and make sure we don't see complaints in syslog about "address in use" (which means that we didn't bind to a new socket, and socket-based activation will no longer work) Change-Id: I32eb761a0f2c0a642ce5a6d9997e959a53c18f13 Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/344932 Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>

net-print/cups: utilize socket-based activation We can now 'start on socket ...', which will allow us to avoid starting/running CUPS for all time. This *should* be pretty straightforward, except that upstart-socket-bridge doesn't do two things right for us: (1) It doesn't create directories, if missing. So we need to make sure /run/cups/ is available before upstart-socket-bridge runs. (2) It doesn't create sockets with the appropriate permissions. We need CUPS's socket to be user-writeable (not just writeable by root). So we need 777, not 755. I've hacked these with pre- and post-start jobs. I made the post-start job retry with a 10 second timeout, in case we race with upstart-socket-bridge (upstart-socket-bridge should *start* before us, but that doesn't guarantee it wins the race to creating our socket). It'd also be nice if upstart could just fixup these things for us... BUG=chromium:616778 TEST=run CUPS command (e.g., `lpstat -W all`) and check for CUPS to start, then stop after some idle timeout TEST=manually test cups-post-upstart-socket-bridge.conf by: # Clear out /run/cups/cups.sock stop upstart-socket-bridge start cups-post-upstart-socket-bridge # Now cups-upstart-socket-bridge will go into a respawn loop, waiting # for /run/cups/cups.sock for a few seconds. # After a few seconds, try... touch /run/cups/cups.sock # ...and see cups-post-upstart-socket-bridge will chmod it to 777 ls -l /run/cups/cups.sock TEST=`test_that <IP> platform_CUPSDaemon` Change-Id: Ie3635c50fb62a3e4fdace607cb2b7dea79429ea0 Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/343273

login: Adjust thread priority limit to -20. This enables chrome/android to renice critical threads to a higher priority. -20 matches ANDROID_PRIORITY_HIGHEST, and Talkback, which is the accessibility component on Android side, actually uses the priority so the component's audio playback for a11y won't be blocked by other ANDROID_PRIORITY_URGENT_AUDIO threads. BUG=b:29124072 TEST=Sign in, enable spoken feedback to start Talkback, confirm that Talkback does not crash.
